jake (eng-platform): Heads-up — I sketched a proposal for an SLO-aware 429/burst dashboard + alert playbook to reduce noise and speed CS handoffs. Sharing for feedback.
eli (eng-sre): nice. main idea?
jake (eng-platform): We already alert on raw 429 spikes which floods SRE and CS. Idea: evaluate alerts against a short-term error budget and only page if we're breaching SLO AND the per-org 429 rate is above a configurable burst multiplier. Otherwise create a low-priority incident or ticket.
maria (eng-sre): agree. We should also factor per-key burst suppression windows so one noisy API key doesn't drown others.
zoe (customer-success): from CS side: we need a clear, short message we can send customers when we see a transient burst vs real quota exhaustion. Template please.
eli (eng-sre): rough thresholds I put in the doc:
```
# pseudo-prometheus
sum(rate(api_responses_total{status="429"}[5m])) by (org) / sum(rate(api_requests_total[5m])) by (org) > 0.03  # org 429 rate > 3% in 5m
AND
total_429_count{org="$ORG"} > 100  # avoid tiny orgs noise
AND
increase(kv_cache_hits_total[10m]) < 10  # heuristic that caching didn't mask it
```
If breach AND error_budget_remaining(org) < 0.5 -> page. Else -> trigger ticket/CS alert.
jake (eng-platform): Also put a burst multiplier: compare current per-key qps to 99th percentile historical qps. If multiplier > 4 we escalate faster.
maria (eng-sre): Can we surface a synthetic "burst score" in the dashboard so operators don't have to reason across 3 panels? Score = weighted(429_rate, burst_multiplier, error_budget_pct).
eli (eng-sre): yes — we can add a single panel and a short hover text explaining components.
zoe (customer-success): for the CS template: short lines, e.g.:
"Hi <name>, we observed a short burst of rate-limiting (429s) on your key from <time> to <time>. We've applied automatic mitigation; if you continue to see 429s please reply and we'll coordinate. Track at <link-to-org-panel>."
zoe (customer-success): include a checkbox list of mitigation steps we can run for them (ramp rules, temporary key throttle, request replay analysis).
jake (eng-platform): ops-bot integrations: when alert is low-priority, create a ticket in zendesk and attach a snapshot of the org panel and top 5 client endpoints. When high-priority, page oncall and ping #eng-sre-pager.
ops-bot: automatic: created ticket #BF-2987 for org acme-corp with attached snapshot.
maria (eng-sre): runbook draft suggestions (short):
1) Confirm 429 surge is not due to a known deploy. Check /deploys last 30m.
2) Check per-key qps and identify top offenders.
3) If high QPS from single key, enable per-key softlimit at 70% of observed peak and notify customer.
4) If many keys, consider adding short global throttle and invoke fallback routing to cheaper model variants.
5) If SLO breach confirmed, escalate to incident channel and start postmortem.
eli (eng-sre): add metric queries to each step and quick commands we can paste. Example quick command to add softlimit: `rbctl quotas set --org $ORG --key $KEY --soft 0.7 --ttl 15m`
maria (eng-sre): +1 also include the exact dashboard links and a single-click "capture snapshot" button in console (product ticket needed).
jake (eng-platform): action items:
- eli: implement burst-score panel and alert rule prototype (ETA 3d)
- maria: add runbook snippets and commands to playbook (ETA 2d)
- zoe: draft CS templates and mitigation checklist (ETA 1d)
- me: create product ticket for snapshot button and link in ops-bot (ETA 1d)
eli (eng-sre): I'll start with the alert rule in staging and post the prometheus rule here.
zoe (customer-success): thanks — I'll prep a short canned response and share with support team for signoff.
jake (eng-platform): if nobody objects I'll create an RFC Monday to formalize thresholds and the error budget integration. Please comment in the doc: https://redwood-internal.internal/doc/ops/slo-burst-playbook (still draft).
maria (eng-sre): no objections. one ask: make sure the alerting UI surfaces the historical 429 trend and the per-key rank in the same tile.
eli (eng-sre): noted. tagging @oncall in high-priority rule so escalation is consistent.
ops-bot: reminder: oncall rotation for week of 2026-08-03: @eli_oncall, @maria_oncall.
jake (eng-platform): perfect. wrapping up — will file RFC Monday and assign tasks. Thanks all :thumbsup:
eli (eng-sre): :+1:
zoe (customer-success): :heart:
